articles.title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
articles.titleEn: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
articles.abstract: Late spring frost is an intensifying climatic disturbance, yet how frost damage to different organs (leaves and flowers) reshapes reproductive phenology and generates carry-over effects remains unclear. Using 259,732 phenological observations across eight European woody species spanning 1950–2024, we show that foliar frost damage shortened the fruit development period (FDP; the interval from flowering to fruit maturity) by 1.6 days, driven by delayed flowering and advanced fruit maturity. Conversely, floral frost damage prolonged FDP by 1.3 days through delayed fruit maturity, with both effects strengthening under greater frost severity. Accounting for anomalously warm conditions in the frost year substantially reduced the estimated delays in flowering and subsequent-year phenology, indicating that neglecting climatic context leads to overestimation of frost effects. These findings reveal organ-specific pathways through which frost damage reshapes reproductive phenology while generating limited carry-over effects, refining current understanding of phenological responses under climate change.

articles.title: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
articles.titleEn: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
articles.abstract: Stature is a key indicator of pediatric health, yet the molecular and metabolic architecture governing childhood growth remains incompletely defined. We conduct genome-wide association analyses of stature from birth to childhood (574,580 measurements; 72,704 Norwegian children) and integrate UK Biobank data (age 10 and adulthood). We uncover life-stage shifts in the genetics of stature, identifying previously not identified childhood-specific effects including variants near GLP1R with BMI-independent effects, and reveal three temporal clusters - Infancy and Childhood clusters enriched for endocrine and metabolic pathways, and a Lifetime growth cluster enriched for skeletal biology. Proteome analysis reveals that prepubertal height is associated with widespread changes in the circulation, identifying 106 height-associated proteins and linking IGF1, IGF2, and IGFBP3 levels to childhood-height polygenic scores. Mendelian randomization shows that reduced fetal growth and taller prepubertal height increase type 2 diabetes risk, independent of adult stature. These findings uncover developmental stage-specific genetic and proteomic influences on child-growth and links to adult metabolic health.

articles.title: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
articles.titleEn: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
articles.abstract: Benzoxaboroles (BoBs) such as acoziborole feature a boron-heterocyclic core and are an important innovation in the development of drugs against a range of pathogens and other pathologies. A broad pharmacological spectrum is associated with chemically diverse BoB derivatives, including multiple modes-of-action (MoA) and molecular targets. However, a consensus MoA for BoBs targeting evolutionarily diverse protozoan pathogens has emerged, with identification of CPSF3 in the CPSF complex as a target in both apicomplexan and kinetoplastida parasites. Here, using comprehensive genetic screens in Trypanosoma brucei , we establish a functional connection between the boron-heterocyclic scaffold shared by all BoBs and protein sumoylation genes. We observe a rapid, transient increase in global protein sumoylation following BoB exposure. While we do not observe direct CPSF3 sumoylation, we find that acoziborole and other BoBs rapidly and specifically destabilise CPSF3 in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

articles.title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
articles.titleEn: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
articles.abstract: Although desmin intermediate filaments are critical for muscle architecture and homeostasis, their spatial 3D organization remains elusive. Their known localization to sarcomeric Z-lines delimits the periodic array of actin and myosin filaments. Here, using d STORM and SIM sub-diffraction resolution microscopy, we resolve the spatial 3D organization of desmin filaments within mouse skeletal muscle, and reveal they are not confined to Z-lines. Our reconstruction reveals that desmin intermediate filaments extend from Z-lines into the sarcomere interior, where they align with actin filaments. Functional assays show that disrupting desmin filament assembly in normal male mouse muscle using a dominant negative inhibitor of desmin selectively reduces active tension at longer sarcomere lengths, indicating a role for desmin in sarcomere mechanics. These findings expand the structural model of the muscle sarcomere and support a role for desmin in force production.

articles.title: Uncovering Nonstationary Dependence Among Drought Drivers: Identification and Modeling for Compound Drought Assessment
articles.titleEn: Uncovering Nonstationary Dependence Among Drought Drivers: Identification and Modeling for Compound Drought Assessment
articles.abstract: Hydrometeorological variables, such as precipitation, soil moisture, and streamflow are widely recognized to exhibit non‐stationarity in their individual time series as human activities and climate change. In contrast, the extent to which the dependence structure linking these variables evolves over time remains poorly understood, despite its importance for characterizing compound droughts. Assuming stationary dependence may therefore obscure key drought dynamics and bias multivariate drought assessment. Hence, we proposes a diagnostic‐driven framework that first investigate and model nonstationary dependence among drought drivers and subsequently develops a Non‐stationary Integrated Drought Index (NIDI) for compound drought assessment. The framework combines a Bayesian dynamic model with Differential Evolution Markov Chain (DE‐MC) inference and a time‐sliding window approach to identify nonstationarity in both marginal drought behavior and intervariable dependence across meteorological, agricultural, and hydrological droughts. The approach is applied to the Krishna River Basin (India), a climatically heterogeneous and drought‐prone region. Results provide clear evidence of time‐varying dependence among precipitation, soil moisture, and streamflow, which is effectively captured by the proposed framework. Accounting for nonstationary dependence improves the identification of historical droughts, including major events in 1985, 1987, 2002–03, and 2012, and enhance detection of compound drought conditions relative to conventional stationary and univariate drought indices. The results demonstrate that evolving dependence plays a critical role in multivariate drought dynamics and that neglecting it can lead to underestimation of drought severity. The proposed framework provides a robust basis for monitoring compound droughts and offers insights for drought risk assessment under nonstationary hydroclimatic conditions.

articles.title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
articles.titleEn: A highly distorted benzenium cation
articles.abstract: In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC + ), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC + with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC + participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC + exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

articles.title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
articles.titleEn: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
articles.abstract: Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Pooled sustained-flux global warming potential (SGWP) was ‒122.41 ± 81.99 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 for natural coastal wetlands and 250.60 ± 101.06 for LULCC sites, corresponding to 0.17 ± 0.06 Gt CO 2 e of cumulative emissions over two decades. The descriptive SGWP contrast with pooled LULCC sites was larger for vegetated wetlands ( + 309.32%) than for tidal flats ( + 165.02%). Ecologically restored wetlands showed negative pooled SGWP ( − 33.03 ± 114.70 mg CO 2 e m ‒2 h ‒1 ), contrasting with the positive pooled LULCC estimate. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

articles.title: Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
articles.titleEn: Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
articles.abstract: Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10 −6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 10 11 photons s −1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.

articles.title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
articles.titleEn: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
articles.abstract: The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

articles.title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
articles.titleEn: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
articles.abstract: As electronic devices are engineered at increasingly smaller length scales, new nanoscopic metrologies are needed. Measuring nanoscale temperatures and pressures is challenging as physical contact inevitably perturbs the system, and collecting far-field thermal radiation limits the spatial resolution. Kikuchi diffraction thermometry (KDTh), a non-contact scanning electron microscope (SEM) technique, can sensitively map nanoscale temperatures. Local lattice changes measured by Kikuchi pattern fitting enable translating volumetric strain to temperature via the material’s coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). Measurements on Joule-heated graphite come from rastering a 5.5-nm electron probe across the sample, achieving a ~ 0.01% fractional precision and 2.2 K/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz temperature sensitivity. KDTh offers superior sensitivity by fitting the entire Kikuchi pattern, instead of a particular Kikuchi band or interband angle. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) techniques can achieve a similar precision, but electron-transparency limits their applications. KDTh can operate in both transmission and reflection modes to cost-effectively accommodate a variety of samples.

articles.title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys
articles.titleEn: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys
articles.abstract: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy–interstitial diffusivity convergence. We develop and validate a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential based on the moment tensor potential formalism for body-centered-cubic Zr–Ti–Nb alloys, enabling accurate large-scale simulations of defect energetics and migration. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a robust inverse correlation between LLD and the activation energy disparity between vacancies and interstitials. This relationship is further validated in face-centered-cubic V–Co–Ni and Ni–Pd systems, demonstrating transferability across distinct chemistries and crystal structures. LLD-induced narrowing of vacancy–interstitial mobility differences promotes Frenkel pair recombination and defect self-healing. Mechanistically, vacancy diffusion is governed by the energy barrier associated with bond-length compression at the saddle state, together with statistical sampling of low-barrier jumps mediated by oversized atoms. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful, physically grounded design lever that links nanoscale disorder to point-defect self-healing, offering a practical pathway for the accelerated discovery of next-generation structural materials for extreme environments.

articles.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
articles.titleEn: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
articles.abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

articles.title: Effects of Aquaculture Ponds on Groundwater Salinization and Submarine Groundwater Discharge in Tidally Influenced Coastal Aquifers
articles.titleEn: Effects of Aquaculture Ponds on Groundwater Salinization and Submarine Groundwater Discharge in Tidally Influenced Coastal Aquifers
articles.abstract: Coastal aquaculture ponds store saline, nutrient‐rich water and can leak into adjacent aquifers, yet their impacts on groundwater salinization and submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) under tidal conditions remain poorly quantified. We use a two‐dimensional variable density groundwater flow and solute transport model to examine how a leaking saline pond interacts with a tidally influenced coastal aquifer. The model tracks the evolution of a pond infiltrated saline plume (ISP) and its interactions with the upper saline plume (USP) and saltwater wedge (SW) for a suite of scenarios spanning tidal amplitude, beach slope, hydraulic conductivity, inland freshwater head, pond water salinity, and pond configuration. We evaluate metrics of salinized areas, SGD partitioning, mixing between ISP, USP and SW and associated changes in saltwater residence times. Results show that pond salinity is the primary control on overall salinization and SGD partitioning, while pond water level and compacted‐soil permeability control how strongly pond leakage perturbs the USP and SW. The presence of the pond generally reduces USP extent and USP‐derived saline SGD, while the SW response depends on pond salinity, changing from slight expansion at low salinity to contraction at high salinity. Importantly, pond‐derived saline water typically overlaps with about 80 percent of the USP area (median across all simulations) and causes reduced saltwater residence times in the USP. These interactions imply that coastal aquaculture ponds can intensify groundwater salinization and reorganize tidally driven saltwater circulation, with important implications for how aquaculture‐derived solutes are transformed and exported to nearshore marine ecosystems via SGD pathways.

articles.title: Characterizing runoff response to rainfall in permafrost catchments and its implications for hydrological and biogeochemical fluxes in a warming climate
articles.titleEn: Characterizing runoff response to rainfall in permafrost catchments and its implications for hydrological and biogeochemical fluxes in a warming climate
articles.abstract: Understanding how Arctic catchments respond to rainfall is critical for anticipating hydrological and biogeochemical effects of a warming climate. We use ensemble rainfall-runoff analysis (ERRA) to identify how runoff response to rainfall varies with meteorological, subsurface, and geomorphic conditions across three permafrost catchments: Upper Kuparuk (Alaska) and the Goose and Ptarmigan catchments (Cape Bounty, Nunavut, Canadian High Arctic). ERRA enables us to quantify event-scale runoff responses to rainfall using high-resolution, multi-year hydrometeorological datasets, and test how variations in rainfall intensity, thaw depth, antecedent effective wetness, and active layer detachments (ALDs) affect runoff behavior. At Upper Kuparuk, our results show that peak runoff response increases by more than five-fold in response to increases in antecedent streamflow (a proxy for antecedent effective wetness), and is also higher in summers with higher average precipitation. By contrast, at the same catchment, warmer winters and springs are associated with reduced runoff sensitivity to rainfall. Furthermore, a paired watershed comparison shows that streamflow and riverine fluxes of dissolved solids, suspended sediment, and particulate organic carbon are more readily mobilized by rainfall inputs when ALDs are present. Considered together, these findings highlight the difficulty in generalizing climate-driven runoff trends in permafrost regions subject to competing and interacting controls, such as precipitation intensity, storage capacity and permafrost stability. Our findings offer a more nuanced alternative to broad classifications of Arctic landscapes as “drying” or “wetting” under climate change.
articles.abstractEn: Understanding how Arctic catchments respond to rainfall is critical for anticipating hydrological and biogeochemical effects of a warming climate. ERRA enables us to quantify event-scale runoff responses to rainfall using high-resolution, multi-year hydrometeorological datasets, and test how variations in rainfall intensity, thaw depth, antecedent effective wetness, and active layer detachments (ALDs) affect runoff behavior. At Upper Kuparuk, our results show that peak runoff response increases by more than five-fold in response to increases in antecedent streamflow (a proxy for antecedent effective wetness), and is also higher in summers with higher average precipitation. By contrast, at the same catchment, warmer winters and springs are associated with reduced runoff sensitivity to rainfall. Furthermore, a paired watershed comparison shows that streamflow and riverine fluxes of dissolved solids, suspended sediment, and particulate organic carbon are more readily mobilized by rainfall inputs when ALDs are present. Considered together, these findings highlight the difficulty in generalizing climate-driven runoff trends in permafrost regions subject to competing and interacting controls, such as precipitation intensity, storage capacity and permafrost stability. Our findings offer a more nuanced alternative to broad classifications of Arctic landscapes as “drying” or “wetting” under climate change.

articles.title: FluidUrban v1.0: enhancing urban ventilation and pollutant dispersion modelling with three-dimensional dynamic adaptive meshes optimisation
articles.titleEn: FluidUrban v1.0: enhancing urban ventilation and pollutant dispersion modelling with three-dimensional dynamic adaptive meshes optimisation
articles.abstract: Simulating urban airflow and pollutant dispersion requires resolving multiscale physical processes, from large-scale meteorological forcing to highly localized building-induced turbulence. To accurately capture these multiscale urban flow fields, this study introduces FluidUrban v1.0, an advanced modelling system built upon the Fluidity solver and centred on a three-dimensional Dynamic Adaptive Mesh Optimization (DAMO) framework. By dynamically adapting mesh resolution in response to the evolution of flow physics and scalar gradients, DAMO concentrates computational resources on critical high-gradient regions such as building wakes, shear layers and scalar sharp plumes. The model's performance is systematically evaluated against high-fidelity “WOTAN” wind-tunnel experimental data under varying surface roughness conditions and inflow directions. The results demonstrate that the FluidUrban with DAMO framework consistently outperforms traditional non-uniform fixed meshes (FIXM) by accurately capturing complex urban wind fields and pollutant concentration. For normalized wind speed, FluidUrban with DAMO achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.187, representing a notable reduction from 0.214 simulated by FIXM. In terms of wind direction, the model reduced the MAE by up to 38.4 % in medium roughness and 36.1 % in high roughness conditions, respectively, during realistic oblique inflow scenarios. Additionally, DAMO effectively mitigates the non-physical numerical dissipation observed in static meshes, significantly improving the prediction of streamwise and lateral turbulence intensities. Furthermore, for pollutant dispersion, the model effectively suppressed numerical diffusion and maintained sharp plume gradients, achieving an 89 % compliance rate with established atmospheric model evaluation standards (FB, NMSE, and MG), compared to only 50 % for FIXM. Although DAMO introduces runtime overhead for mesh regeneration, this cost is justified by significant gains in physical accuracy and multi-scale flow resolution. Following the systematic evaluation, FluidUrban v1.0 was applied to a realistic urban scenario, demonstrating its robust capability to resolve the complex flow fields and spatial heterogeneity within real urban morphologies. Thus, FluidUrban v1.0 demonstrates to be a robust aerodynamic tool for resolving the transient, small-scale flow structures critical to pollutant transport, establishing a solid foundation for the future integration of comprehensive urban physical components, including radiation, vegetation, and full energy-balance physics.

articles.title: The 4-mode Modal Aerosol Module in C+ + (MAM4xx) v1.0: representing prognostic aerosols in a global cloud-system resolving atmosphere model for GPU exascale computing
articles.titleEn: The 4-mode Modal Aerosol Module in C+ + (MAM4xx) v1.0: representing prognostic aerosols in a global cloud-system resolving atmosphere model for GPU exascale computing
articles.abstract: Aerosols are a key component of Earth system models since they affect meteorology and the Earth's energy budget through complex cloud-aerosol-radiation interactions. Over the past decade, Earth system models have increased their spatial resolution to better resolve atmospheric processes; however, this advancement comes with significantly higher computational costs. To address this issue, some models now take advantage of high-performance Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) exascale computer clusters which offer faster processing capabilities with a higher level of parallelism than traditional Central Processing Unit (CPU) systems, but these models still lack detailed representations of aerosols. In this study, we describe the development of a new GPU-enabled prognostic aerosol model based on the four-mode version of the Modal Aerosol Module (MAM4), called MAM4xx, that has been coupled to the Energy Exascale Earth System (E3SM) Atmospheric Model (EAM) in C++ (EAMxx). To the best of our knowledge, MAM4xx is the first fully GPU-enabled aerosol model with sophisticated process representations. MAM4 has been completely rewritten in C++ using the Kokkos performance-portability programming library while preserving all the physical and chemical processes in the original Fortran version. The Kokkos library ensures compatibility across GPUs from various vendors and thus enables execution on multiple GPU exascale high-performance computer clusters. We describe the steps undertaken to port the code to C++/Kokkos as well as the rigorous testing methodology (i.e., unit tests, real-world tests) so that the functionality remains intact and that bugs were not inadvertently introduced. We demonstrate that MAM4xx coupled within EAMxx with ∼12 km horizontal grid spacing behaves as expected for real-world conditions based on comparison with observations and a reanalysis aerosol dataset over the central U.S. during the spring of 2016. Currently, MAM4xx increases the computational cost of the host atmospheric model by ∼40 %, which is due primarily to the treatment of aerosol-cloud interactions, highlighting the need to optimize these processes for GPU computational efficiency. Future improvements to MAM4xx will benefit from recent advancements in the physical representation of aerosols in MAM4 as they are ported to C++/Kokkos. Additional testing for longer periods of time to encompass a wider range of atmospheric conditions, over other geographic regions, and at higher spatial resolution will be conducted in the future to more robustly assess simulated aerosol properties.

articles.title: Species-resolved inventory of forest biogenic volatile organic emissions across China with MEGAN v3.2
articles.titleEn: Species-resolved inventory of forest biogenic volatile organic emissions across China with MEGAN v3.2
articles.abstract: Biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) are important precursors of secondary organic aerosols and tropospheric ozone, yet their emissions are commonly modelled at the plant functional type (PFT) level, which obscures substantial interspecies variability. This limitation is particularly acute for China, where high forest diversity and ambitious afforestation initiatives are expected to reshape national BVOC budgets. Here, we present a species-resolved BVOC emissions inventory for China covering 234 tree species (Liu et al., 2026). The inventory was developed within the Model of Emissions of Gases and Aerosols from Nature (MEGAN) v3.2 modeling framework, with refined inputs comprising species-specific emission factors and high-resolution forest composition data for China. Total forest BVOC emissions were estimated at 10.26 Tg of compound mass in 2019, with summer emissions accounting for about 50 % of the annual total and a clear decreasing gradient from southern to northern China. Emissions were highly concentrated among a limited number of species: the five largest contributors, Pinus massoniana , Quercus liaotungensis , Phyllostachys edulis , Cunninghamia lanceolata , and Quercus variabilis accounted for 41.7 % of total emissions while occupying only 25.4 % of forest area. At the compound-class level, Quercus liaotungensis dominated isoprene emissions, whereas Pinus massoniana was the leading contributor to monoterpene emissions. Applying this species-resolved framework to two future afforestation scenarios with identical planted areas but contrasting species composition, we found that BVOC emissions may increase by 4.65 Tg yr −1 with the biomass-maximization tree species and by 5.10 Tg yr −1 under the most environmental-suitability species. Notably, the dominant component of additional BVOC emissions shifts from isoprene under biomass maximization (BIO) to monoterpenes under highest environmental suitability (HIGH). These results demonstrate the importance of incorporating species-specific emission traits into BVOC models and suggest that future afforestation strategies could substantially reshape both the magnitude and chemical composition of biogenic emissions, with implications for atmospheric chemistry and air quality depending on species selection.

articles.title: A multi-decadal dataset of surface damage on Antarctic ice shelves (1999–2024)
articles.titleEn: A multi-decadal dataset of surface damage on Antarctic ice shelves (1999–2024)
articles.abstract: Many Antarctic ice shelves have undergone accelerated thinning and retreat in recent decades, weakening their buttressing effect on grounded ice and increasing the risk of further sea-level rise. Surface damage, including crevasses, rifts and heavily fractured areas, is an important indicator of ice shelf structural integrity, but there is limited understanding of its long-term evolution across Antarctic ice shelves. Here we present a new surface damage dataset for nine representative Antarctic ice shelves, derived from Landsat optical imagery covering the period 1999–2024. These ice shelves include Amery, Brunt, Crosson, Dotson, Holmes, Pine Island, Scar Inlet, Thwaites and Totten, and encompass a range of change behaviours from relatively stable to rapidly changing systems. A deep-learning image segmentation model was trained on a manually annotated dataset from diverse Antarctic ice shelves to automatically map surface damage. To extend the usable record, Landsat 7 scan-line-corrector-off imagery was restored using a diffusion-model-based framework fine-tuned for Antarctic imagery. The final dataset contains 170 surface damage maps at 30 m resolution, each representing a single ice shelf for a specific year. Temporal coverage varies among ice shelves owing to differences in the availability of usable imagery. Evaluation on two independent test sets indicates that the model generalizes well across spatially distinct and cross-sensor settings. The dataset demonstrates good multi-temporal consistency, supporting its use for time-series analysis. Among the nine ice shelves, Pine Island, Thwaites and Scar Inlet show the most pronounced surface damage changes during the study period. Compared with existing studies, this dataset provides improved temporal continuity over multi-decadal timescales at substantially finer spatial resolution, offering new insights into the long-term evolution of Antarctic ice shelves and contributing to a better understanding of ice shelf instability. The dataset is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20425951 (Tang et al., 2026a).

articles.title: 4D Aviation Emission Inventory Data of China estimated with QAR data in 2023 (4D-AEID-2023)
articles.titleEn: 4D Aviation Emission Inventory Data of China estimated with QAR data in 2023 (4D-AEID-2023)
articles.abstract: Accurate aviation emission inventories provide the fundamental basis for environmental impact assessment, yet existing estimates typically rely on idealized trajectory assumptions and generic aircraft performance models. Here, we present a high-resolution, four-dimensional aviation emission inventory for purely domestic civil aviation flights within mainland China in 2023, built directly from onboard Quick Access Recorder (QAR) measurements covering 4.52 million flights (∼96.8 % of national commercial movements). Integrating 1 Hz per-engine fuel-flow measurements with observed flight trajectories, ambient temperature and pressure, and specific humidity profiles via the Boeing Fuel Flow Method 2 and atmospheric corrections, this dataset yields temporally and spatially explicit emission estimates for CO 2 , NO x , SO 2 , PM, CO, and HC. In 2023, domestic civil aviation consumed 23.7 Mt of fuel, emitting 74.6 Mt CO 2 , 311.84 kt NO x , 73.5 kt CO, 6.02 kt HC, 23.69 kt SO 2 , and 2.00 kt PM. articles.title: The ICOS Ecosystem Station Loobos: a pine forest site exposed to atmospheric pollution
articles.titleEn: The ICOS Ecosystem Station Loobos: a pine forest site exposed to atmospheric pollution
articles.abstract: The Loobos Ecosystem Station (ICOS: NL-Loo) is in a pine forest on sandy soil, the most dominant forest type in the Netherlands. The station was first built in 1995 and the first atmospheric flux measurements were taken in 1997. The station was one of the first in EuroFlux and FLUXNET. Between 2021 and 2023, the station was rebuilt to meet the ICOS standards as an Ecosystem Class 2 station. The initial purpose of the station was to measure fluxes of heat, water and carbon dioxide. Over time, interest has increased in better understanding the forest water use and ecosystem dynamics and its interaction with air quality. This has resulted in additional concentration and flux measurements of ozone and volatile organic compounds. In the near future, we intend to include measurements of nitrogen species (ammonia and nitrogen oxides) to exploit Loobos' unique location downwind of major anthropogenic emission hotspots. Documenting the instrumentation and exploring the quality of the data is important to understand the observational data. This paper therefore describes the station in terms of geography, ecosystem and instrumentation. DOIs to all described data are provided in the data availability section.

articles.title: SMHIGridClim, 2.5 km resolution gridded climatology of Fennoscandia
articles.titleEn: SMHIGridClim, 2.5 km resolution gridded climatology of Fennoscandia
articles.abstract: SMHIGridClim, the Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute Gridded Climatology, covers Fennoscandia at 2.5 km horizontal grid resolution for the period 1961–2018. It includes 2 m temperature and two-metre relative humidity at 1, 3, or 6 h temporal resolution (which varies over the covered period), as well as daily minimum and maximum temperatures, daily precipitation, and daily snow depth. The gridding is performed using optimal interpolation with the open-source software gridpp from the Norwegian Meteorological Institute. Observations used in the analysis are provided by the Swedish, Finnish, and Norwegian meteorological institutes, as well as the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Quality control of the observations is conducted using the open-source software TITAN, also developed at the Norwegian Meteorological Institute. The first guess for the optimal interpolation is obtained from the UERRA-HARMONIE reanalysis at 11 km horizontal grid resolution, which is statistically downscaled to fit a subset of the operational ensemble numerical prediction system at 2.5 km horizontal grid resolution, with daily and yearly variations in the downscaling parameters. The quality of the analysis varies over time and depends on both the accuracy of forecasts and the quality and density of available observations. In terms of annual mean root mean square error (RMSE), the quality of SMHIGridClim is comparable to similar gridded datasets covering the Nordic countries. SMHIGridClim is available at https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/ZFZL6K (Andersson et al., 2025).

articles.title: SISAL_monv1: a global database of cave monitoring observations
articles.titleEn: SISAL_monv1: a global database of cave monitoring observations
articles.abstract: Cave monitoring is the process of collecting observational data such as microclimate conditions, hydrogeochemistry and water movement in cave systems. The most common motivation is for speleothem science – the reconstruction of past climate and environmental variability from cave formations such as stalagmites. Applications also include the monitoring of potential recharge to aquifers, as well as cave conservation. PAGES-SISAL (Past Global Changes – Speleothem Isotope Synthesis and AnaLysis), an international working group focused on speleothem science, has created a new global database of cave monitoring data consisting of drip rates and drip water isotopes, and the modern carbonate precipitates that form from these drip waters (so called farmed carbonates, grown on artificial substrates). Moreover, we report meteoric precipitation amounts and water isotopes at or near to cave sites. The database is available at https://doi.org/10.5158/ARP/29W5J3 (Treble et al., 2026). Access to the database is also supported via the SISAL webApp at http://geochem.hu/SISAL_webApp (last access: 12 November 2026). The database contains datasets from 75 caves, with summary information including meta-data on location, elevation, cave depth, lithology, measurement methods and citations for original publications. Speleothem records previously curated by SISAL in SISAL speleothem database versions and corresponding to monitored drip sites are also identified in the new SISAL monitoring database. To supplement observational data gaps and provide accessible and consistent climate data for users, surface climate (precipitation, evaporation, temperature) and meteoric water isotope data extracted from global climate model products are also included in the database.

articles.title: Contrasting Fire‐Driven Erosion Processes Mobilise Distinct Organic Carbon Pools in Forest Landscapes
articles.titleEn: Contrasting Fire‐Driven Erosion Processes Mobilise Distinct Organic Carbon Pools in Forest Landscapes
articles.abstract: Wildfires can substantially alter organic carbon (C) cycling in forest ecosystems beyond immediate emissions from fuel combustion. Among these post‐fire effects, lateral C mobilisation by water erosion is an important but poorly quantified flux, rarely incorporated into fire‐related C budgets. Here, we quantified and characterised C mobilised by hillslope erosion and channel erosion by debris flows in highly fire‐prone eucalypt forests in southeastern Australia. We monitored suspended and bedload C export from headwater catchments across fire severities until erosion returned to background levels, quantified C mobilisation from colluvium by debris flows, characterised C chemical recalcitrance in ash, soils, eroded sediments and colluvium, and constrained colluvial C age using radiocarbon measurements. We then upscaled these fluxes to the area affected by the 2009 Beechworth Fire. Over the three‐year post‐fire perturbation period, hillslope and channel erosion mobilised 15,866 t C (0.78 t C ha −1 ). Hillslope erosion accounted for 91% of this landscape‐scale flux, compared with 9% from debris flows. The two processes mobilised contrasting C pools. Hillslope C export was dominated by young wildfire ash derived from incompletely combusted vegetation and the surface organic soil horizon. In contrast, debris flows generated substantial localised C pulses by eroding deeper colluvial deposits, with 2%–20% of mobilised C older than 6000 years. Chemically recalcitrant and highly recalcitrant forms accounted for 47%–60% of C in fire‐affected hillslope sediments and 43%–74% in colluvium, highlighting the potential importance of these lateral fluxes for long‐term C dynamics. Post‐fire erosion mobilised C equivalent to only approximately 4% of direct fire C emissions, but the C mobilised during the three‐year post‐fire period was equivalent to approximately 210 years of background (unburnt) erosion. Thus, lateral erosion represents an additional and compositionally distinct pathway of fire‐driven C redistribution that should be considered in fire‐prone forest C budgets.

articles.title: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements
articles.titleEn: Building a random forest machine learning model for annual Net Ecosystem Exchange estimation in agricultural fields using discontinuous atmospheric Eddy Covariance measurements
articles.abstract: Atmospheric CO 2 exchanges in agroecosystems are strongly controlled by plant phenology, management and microclimatic conditions; yet obtaining finely resolved flux estimates across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes remains challenging. This study evaluates the ability of a single Eddy Covariance (EC) system combined with wind-sector partitioning and Random Forest (RF) modelling to estimate the annual Net Ecosystem Exchange (NEE) of adjacent fields (wheat, mixed-grain, permanent grassland) in the Marais poitevin wetland (French Atlantic coast). Fluxes were measured over the period 1 February 2023–31 January 2024 and attributed to eight wind sectors, each used as a proxy for the corresponding field or landscape feature that dominates its footprint. Two modelling strategies were compared (i) a single global RF trained on all sectors and (ii) sector-specific RFs trained separately for each wind sector. RF models globally showed good overall performance ( R 2 ≈0.20–0.94 depending on sector and period), but this apparent equivalence broke down once fluxes were reconstructed over the full annual cycle: the sector-specific approach then better reproduced phenological dynamics and management-driven flux reversals (harvest, senescence) than the global model, which compressed inter-sector variability by up to 70 %. Annual NEE estimated from the sector-specific models indicated that the mixed-grain field acted as net source (+151 g C m −2 yr −1 ), whereas the permanent grassland and the wheat field acted as net sinks (−145 and −308 g C m −2 yr −1 , respectively). A light-response-curve partitioning of these reconstructed fluxes into gross primary production (GPP) and ecosystem respiration (Reco) revealed contrasting phenological signatures behind different land-covers. Methodology and associated limitations/uncertainties due to flux measurement and modelling, footprint attribution and sector delineation, and the limited one-year observation period are particularly addressed. This study highlights the novelty and practical value of coupling a single EC system with wind-sector partitioning and machine learning approaches to resolve carbon fluxes at the field scale within heterogeneous agricultural landscapes. This integrated approach provides an alternative to traditional multi-tower setups, offering new opportunities to monitor spatial carbon dynamics and management effects in real agricultural mosaics. Beyond methodological innovation, this work provides one of the first field-scale, uncertainty-resolved carbon flux datasets for a mosaic of contrasting agricultural land covers monitored by a single EC tower, offering a transferable framework to better constrain the terrestrial carbon balance of retro-littoral wet and agricultural landscapes.

articles.title: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest
articles.titleEn: Evaluating GNSS-T VOD sensitivity to plant water dynamics, rainfall interception, and dew in a coniferous forest
articles.abstract: Monitoring forest canopy water is essential for understanding drought response and interception losses under climate change. At short timescales, canopy water is partitioned among internal plant water storage ( S p ), rainfall interception ( S i ), and dew ( S d ), which together regulate plant functioning, canopy evaporation, and precipitation partitioning, yet are rarely observed simultaneously. GNSS transmissometry (GNSS-T) has recently emerged as a low-cost, continuous, stand-scale method to observe L-band vegetation optical depth (VOD) from signal attenuation. However, interpreting GNSS-T VOD remains difficult because the signal integrates multiple water pools and is similarly affected by biomass, canopy structure, and measurement noise. Here, we applied GNSS-T in a mature Picea abies stand in Tharandt, Germany, during the 2024 growing season to separate canopy water storage into S i , S d , and S p . Rainfall interception was simulated with the multilayer Penman-Rutter model CanWat and used to calibrate the empirical VOD to water storage relationship and to convert the GNSS-T noise floor into an equivalent storage detectability threshold. GNSS-T VOD tracked interception storage robustly and approximately linearly at both 30 min and event scales (R2=0.63/0.81), and modeled S i explained VOD variability better than gross precipitation alone. The inferred attenuation coefficient b was comparable in magnitude to reported L-band values and showed a seasonal variation, which we accounted for with monthly binned calibrations of b . Dew-related wetting signals were distinguishable in VOD and yielded plausible mean nightly amounts, while the largest predictions exceeded reported values and physical boundaries, which we attribute to residual noise in the VOD data. Diurnal changes in internal plant water storage were not directly detectable at sub-daily and daily scales, indicating that variations in S p remained below the GNSS-T noise floor during the study period, as shown with trait-based estimates of maximum plant water loss. This storage-versus-noise framework provides a practical way to benchmark the hydraulic sensitivity of GNSS-T across sites that differ in biomass, hydraulic strategy, and climate, and further highlights noise reduction as a prerequisite for plant-hydraulic applications. This study further promotes GNSS-T VOD as a robust monitoring instrument for resolving sub-event interception storage, a potential avenue for constraining hydrological models.

articles.title: Climate warming-induced agricultural nitrous oxide emissions can offset mitigation benefits of fertiliser reduction
articles.titleEn: Climate warming-induced agricultural nitrous oxide emissions can offset mitigation benefits of fertiliser reduction
articles.abstract: Agriculture is the dominant source of anthropogenic nitrous oxide (N 2 O), a potent greenhouse gas with a high global warming potential. In Switzerland, substantial changes in fertiliser use alongside climatic conditions have occurred over the past four decades, yet the relative contributions of management practices versus environmental change to long-term N 2 O emission trends remain incompletely understood. Here, we applied the biogeochemical model DayCent at 1 km resolution across Switzerland, integrating spatially explicit datasets on climate, soil properties and agricultural management, to quantify N 2 O emissions for the period 1981–2020 from croplands and grasslands and attribute emission changes to management versus climate drivers. Simulated national N 2 O emissions from agricultural soils declined by roughly 5 % from 4.0 to 3.8 kt N yr −1 between the 1980s and 2010s, primarily due to a 25 % reduction in N fertiliser use. Our attribution simulations suggested that under real climate conditions, such a decrease in fertiliser N inputs (−25 %) over the period studied lowered emissions by 15.2 % in croplands and by 12.0 % in grasslands (including permanent meadows and pastures, and high alpine summer pastures). However, compared to a control scenario (in the absence of climate change), rising temperatures over the past 40 years offset these gains, increasing emissions by 5.7 % in croplands and 13.6 % in grasslands. These results show that warming-induced N 2 O emissions partially negate mitigation from improved fertiliser management, highlighting the need for integrated agricultural N 2 O mitigation strategies to meet emission reduction targets under future warming.

articles.title: Numerical analysis of dynamics between debris flows and wave propagation using multi-layer shallow water equations
articles.titleEn: Numerical analysis of dynamics between debris flows and wave propagation using multi-layer shallow water equations
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Debris flows are destructive disasters that often cause casualties and property damage, particularly when occurring near residential areas. In reservoir basins, debris flows can reduce effective storage capacity by raising the dead storage level and generate waves that may induce overtopping or structural collapse. Previous numerical studies have applied three-dimensional (3D) hydrodynamics or smoothed particle hydrodynamics to analyze debris flow-induced waves. However, these studies focused on the direct inflow of soil masses into water, without accounting for erosion and entrainment processes. As a result, they have limitations in simulating debris generated in upland areas that undergo erosion and entrainment before entering reservoirs. To address this gap, we developed a one-dimensional (1D) multi-layer simulation model based on shallow water equations that explicitly considers erosion, entrainment, and deposition. The model was validated through theoretical analysis and a laboratory experiment, and applied to the 2020 Sanyang Reservoir collapse event in South Korea. Scenario-based simulations were performed under varying debris flow characteristics and reservoir water levels. The results demonstrate that debris flow momentum strongly correlates with the scale of generated waves, with maximum momentum serving as a reliable predictor of wave magnitude. This study offers a practical framework for assessing debris flow impacts on dam and reservoir safety.

articles.title: COHESION: a connectivity-based framework for evaluating landslide susceptibility, runout hazards, and hillslope–channel coupling
articles.titleEn: COHESION: a connectivity-based framework for evaluating landslide susceptibility, runout hazards, and hillslope–channel coupling
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Landslides hinder sustainable development in mountain regions by threatening livelihoods and damaging linear and water infrastructure. Susceptibility maps are widely used to identify landslide hazards, yet they usually omit hillslope connectivity. This is a critical shortcoming for mapping the magnitude of landslides, for identifying cascading hazards, and for understanding landslide contributions to fluvial sediment budgets. We introduce COHESION (COnnected HillslopE SusceptibIlity for slOpe failure and ruNout), a framework for coupling pixel-level susceptibility mapping approaches with connectivity analysis to identify downslope-connected landslide objects (LSOs), associated runout pathways and runout intersections with river networks. For the 7573 km 2 Kaligandaki Basin in Nepal, we base COHESION on a factor-of-safety assessment with probabilistic rainfall forcing and identify 1.06 million potential LSOs. Of these, 690 000 LSOs have nonzero precipitation-exceedance probabilities and cover 31.0 % of the basin. Precipitation-exceedance probabilities imply an annualized failure potential equivalent to 4.9 % of the basin area. Based on these probabilities, we propose that sediment mobilization from landsliding is constrained by soil-production and soil-mantle recovery rates rather than by triggering rainfall, a constraint hidden by typical susceptibility maps that do not account for failure volumes and probabilities. Considering runout pathways increases the mapped landslide-hazard footprint by 53.3 %. 29.7 % of buildings and 66.8 % of road segments are located on LSOs, while 20.7 % of buildings and 16.3 % of roads are on runout pathways. 35.3 % of LSOs connect to the river network, linking slope failures and river channels at more than 30 000 locations. Both results highlight the need to include connectivity and runout in geohazard screening and fluvial sediment budgets. COHESION's connectivity-based approach can improve the basin-scale screening of landslide hazards to settlements, roads, and water infrastructure, while also linking slope failure to sediment delivery in mountain rivers.

articles.title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
articles.titleEn: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
articles.abstract: To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of Homo sapiens , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and H. sapiens lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of H. sapiens remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and H. sapiens dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

articles.title: Sequential anion chemistry enables dynamic interphase regulation in high-voltage LiCoO 2
articles.titleEn: Sequential anion chemistry enables dynamic interphase regulation in high-voltage LiCoO 2
articles.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries using LiCoO 2 cathodes have powered portable electronics for decades, yet their operation above 4.5 volts remains severely constrained by the unstable evolution of the cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI). Under high-voltage conditions, lattice oxygen release and continuous electrolyte oxidation progressively degrade interfacial integrity. Here, we report a diluent-mediated local solvation regulation strategy to decrease dissociative solvent molecules and induce dual anion selective redistribution around Li + , forming a sequential solvation motif that drives sequential anion interfacial chemistry. DFOB − preferentially decomposes to establish a robust initial CEI framework, while BF 4 − continuously drives interfacial reactions to dynamically repair CEI defects and quench reactive oxygen species generated from lattice oxygen release. This dynamic regulation mechanism effectively stabilizes LiCoO 2 under aggressive high-voltage cycling. Consequently, the LiCoO 2 cathode delivers stable performance for 500 cycles at 4.5 volts with 73.5% capacity retention even in a low-concentration ether-based electrolyte. Furthermore, graphite||LiCoO 2 pouch cell achieves an energy density of 265.8 watt-hours per kilogram and exhibits favorable low-temperature resilience, retaining 99.1% capacity after 700 cycles at −20°C. These findings provide critical mechanistic insights into how solvation structure–driven anion chemistry can govern interfacial stability and unlock high-voltage, extreme-condition lithium-ion batteries.

articles.title: DFT-assisted natural abundance 13 C zero-field NMR via optical magnetometry
articles.titleEn: DFT-assisted natural abundance 13 C zero-field NMR via optical magnetometry
articles.abstract: Zero-field (ZF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy probes nuclear J-couplings without homogeneous magnetic fields, enabling inexpensive and geometrically flexible detection, including through metal. However, its broader use for chemical analysis has been limited by sensitivity and the difficulty of predicting the dense ZF multiplets. Here we demonstrate natural-abundance (1.1%) carbon-13 ( 13 C) ZF spectroscopy on off-the-shelf liquids using a compact commercial rubidium-87 magnetometer without hyperpolarization or special preparation. Instrumental advances yield improved sensitivity, ≤250-millihertz linewidths, and >week-long stability, enabling isotopomer-resolved fingerprint spectra across a 13-molecule library, including rare (0.0121%) doubly 13 C-labeled species. In parallel, we demonstrate vibrationally corrected density functional theory (DFT) prediction of ZF spectra with good qualitative agreement. Comparing experiment with these calculations renders residual deviations as chemically informative, reporting on hydrogen bonding and ion pairing at high ionic strength. These results contribute toward DFT-assisted ZF NMR as a general platform for field constraint–free molecular identification and for extracting transient solution-state structure from responsive J-coupling observables.

articles.title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
articles.titleEn: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
articles.abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

articles.title: Enzymatic degradation of a polyester-based thermoset composite resin by an engineered cutinase from Fusarium solani
articles.titleEn: Enzymatic degradation of a polyester-based thermoset composite resin by an engineered cutinase from Fusarium solani
articles.abstract: Thermoset composites have become indispensable high-performance materials across key industrial sectors. However, existing recycling methods have yet to deliver sustainable end-of-life solutions for these materials. Here, we report the engineering of a highly active and stable biocatalyst capable of depolymerizing polyester-based thermoset composites. First, a second-generation polyester resin was designed to enhance susceptibility to enzymatic attack. Cutinase from Fusarium solani was selected and subsequently engineered through a combination of directed evolution and computational design using two soluble surrogate motifs representative of the redesigned resin structure. The resulting variant, which incorporated 19 mutations, exhibited a 22-fold increase in activity and an 11°C improvement in melting temperature while achieving recombinant production titers at the gram-per-liter scale in yeast cultivated in fed-batch bioreactor. This engineered enzyme depolymerized the polyester resin with a total release of 6 mM (∼1.08 grams per liter) monomethyl phthalate. Together, to our knowledge, these findings constitute the first documented example of enzymatic degradation of a complex polyester resin from thermoset composite materials.

articles.title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
articles.titleEn: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
articles.abstract: Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) imprint gravitational signatures on the matter within their sphere of influence (SoI). Nuclear gas dynamics can hence be used to accurately measure the mass of an SMBH, yet these measurements remain elusive in the early universe. We report the first dynamical measurement of an SMBH mass at z > 2, based on high–spatial resolution observations of the ionized-carbon 157.7-micrometer and carbon monoxide (12-11) 216.93-micrometer emission lines that resolve the SoI in an obscured quasar at z = 4.6. The radial profile of the velocity dispersion reveals a clear Keplerian rise, requiring the presence of an ∼6 × 10 9 –solar mass SMBH. We propose that heavily obscured quasars allow such tracers to survive in the inner regions and may be ideal targets for increasing dynamical SMBH mass estimates in the early universe.

articles.title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
articles.titleEn: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
articles.abstract: To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in Drosophila to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

articles.title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
articles.titleEn: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
articles.abstract: Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr 2+ –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

articles.title: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
articles.titleEn: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
articles.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Simulations suggested that winter MHWs could generally benefit growth, while summer MHWs produced generally negative impacts, especially at higher latitudes where species experience summer growth periods. When combined, winter and summer MHW scenarios indicated a cumulative negative effect for most species. Vulnerability was highest at the warm- and cold-range edges of species’ distributions. These simulations suggest that temperature-dependent growth may be closely linked to the seasonal timing and frequency of extreme events, with multi-season MHWs posing potential challenges for mariculture species in the future. Our simulations highlight the importance of considering multi-season impacts in climate adaptation strategies.

articles.title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
articles.titleEn: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
articles.abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

articles.title: Assessing Regional Projections of Marine Climatic Impact‐Drivers Using Coordinated Ensembles: Framework and Application to the Mediterranean Sea
articles.titleEn: Assessing Regional Projections of Marine Climatic Impact‐Drivers Using Coordinated Ensembles: Framework and Application to the Mediterranean Sea
articles.abstract: The Mediterranean Sea is among the most climate‐sensitive regions globally, having experienced unprecedented sea surface temperatures, intensified marine heatwaves, and associated ecosystem impacts in recent years. These changes are projected to intensify throughout the 21st century, with implications for marine ecosystems, biogeochemical processes, and coastal societies. Here, we provide a transferable framework for assessing marine climatic impact‐drivers (CIDs) based on key physical ocean essential climate variables, integrating model evaluation, simulation filtering, and confidence assessment of projected changes across global warming levels. The framework is applied to the Mediterranean Sea using a coordinated ensemble of 29 multi‐decadal simulations from high‐resolution regional climate system models participating in Med‐CORDEX. A novel set of marine CIDs is assessed across warming levels from 1.5°C to 4°C, encompassing mean and extreme ocean temperature, mean ocean salinity, vertical stratification, and wind‐driven ocean dynamics at basin, sub‐basin, and coastal scales. Overall, model responses broadly align with historical trends, increasing confidence in projected changes. Projections indicate robust increases in mean ocean temperature, warm extremes, and stratification across regions as warming intensifies. Under high warming levels, extreme warm events become near‐yearly occurrences, whereas cold spells virtually disappear. In contrast, projected changes in salinity, wind stress extremes, and coastal upwelling remain comparatively uncertain across most regions. Beyond the Mediterranean, the proposed framework provides a consistent basis for assessing marine climate risks in other regions as high‐resolution regional projections become available, while remaining adaptable to new indicators. To facilitate the exploration of Mediterranean CID projections, an interactive web tool is provided.

articles.title: Advancing Sub‐Surface Hydrology Through WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW Coupling: Interface Structure and Showcase Demonstration
articles.titleEn: Advancing Sub‐Surface Hydrology Through WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW Coupling: Interface Structure and Showcase Demonstration
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Conventional land surface models (LSMs) have evolved to represent detailed physics for many aspects of water flow and transport but still suffer from missing/simplified processes at the (lower) subsurface boundary. These gaps limit ability to simulate sub‐surface and surface water and energy fluxes. We present a dynamic framework for coupling of the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) MODFLOW, an open‐source hydrologic model representing subsurface hydrology, to WRF‐Hydro, a predominantly surface‐water‐focused hydrologic modeling system. The Basic Model Interface (BMI) coupling standard is used to communicate information between the hydrologic process components of WRF‐Hydro (i.e., the Noah‐Multiparameterization (Noah‐MP) and surface routing modules) and the MODFLOW groundwater component. The BMI functions initialize WRF‐Hydro and MODFLOW simulations, update model states and fluxes (passing groundwater recharge and discharge between WRF‐Hydro and MODFLOW), and finalize the run. The USGS National Groundwater Model, a calibrated steady‐state MODFLOW model, is used as the baseline groundwater model in simulations. The new coupled WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW model is tested over the Republican and Delaware River basins, contrasting test beds with different climates and surface water‐groundwater coupling and complexities. The dynamics of the coupled framework are assessed through tracking changes in hydrologic processes. Two‐way WRF‐Hydro/MODFLOW coupling increased deep‐soil moisture retention and surface evapotranspiration, particularly in low‐relief areas. Groundwater dynamics were largely controlled by transient recharge from WRF‐Hydro highlighting the value of integrated modeling for capturing spatiotemporal hydrologic variability. This modeling effort seeks to advance the representation of groundwater in land and hydrological models and to improve the quantification of groundwater‐soil‐atmosphere and groundwater‐surface water interactions.

articles.title: Comparative Evaluation of Low‐Flow Estimation Performance in Noah‐MP for Improved Hydrological Modeling Across the United States
articles.titleEn: Comparative Evaluation of Low‐Flow Estimation Performance in Noah‐MP for Improved Hydrological Modeling Across the United States
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Accurately simulating low flows is essential for effective water resource management and ecosystem conservation. This study evaluates five runoff and groundwater configurations in the Noah‐MP land surface model—SIMGM, SIMTOP, Schaake96, BATS, and the newly integrated Groundwater for Ungauged Basins (GrUB)—across 543 minimally disturbed reference basins in the contiguous United States. GrUB represents groundwater discharge using a representative‐hillslope formulation with independently derived watershed‐scale parameters and no basin‐specific streamflow calibration. Model performance was assessed using Kling‐Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Nash‐Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and bias under general and low‐flow conditions, identified by the 80% exceedance flows () and Tennant method (). Results indicate no configuration performed best across all metrics. During low‐flow periods, Schaake96 consistently produced the lowest MAE and bias, while GrUB generally ranked second and outperformed SIMGM, SIMTOP, and BATS under both low‐flow definitions. Over the full simulation period, GrUB showed comparatively strong overall performance and the lowest median bias. Spatially, the five configurations generally overestimated low flows in many central and eastern basins, whereas localized underestimation occurred in portions of the Midwest and western United States. Overall, Schaake96 showed the strongest low‐flow performance, while GrUB provided relatively small low‐flow errors and balanced overall performance using independently derived parameters without basin‐specific streamflow calibration. These results highlight substantial differences among Noah‐MP runoff and groundwater configurations and their representation of low‐flow processes.

articles.title: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
articles.titleEn: A neural code for generative speech production in human Wernicke’s area
articles.abstract: Wernicke’s area in the posterior temporal lobe is classically defined by its role in speech comprehension, yet a paradox remains: Why does damage here also profoundly impair speech production? Using direct human brain recordings, cortical stimulation, and lesion analysis, we found that this region is not solely for perception. A discrete subzone within Wernicke’s area, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus (lpSTG), becomes active before speech, is causally necessary for speech production, and codes features of whole upcoming words rather than low-level acoustics or articulatory information. Its neural activity is distinct from the auditory-feedback responses nearby and can decode intended speech in people with paralysis. Thus, while Wernicke’s area is a key part of auditory cortex, it contains a dedicated subregion for speech generation.

articles.title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
articles.titleEn: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
articles.abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

articles.title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
articles.titleEn: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
articles.abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.
