articles.title: Growing-season variability and environmental controls of CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude terrestrial ecosystems
articles.titleEn: Growing-season variability and environmental controls of CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude terrestrial ecosystems
articles.abstract: Rapid warming and accelerating ecological change across high-latitude (>66° N) terrestrial environments are reshaping greenhouse gas dynamics. However, spatiotemporal patterns and environmental drivers of CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes in high-latitude ecosystems remain poorly understood. In this study we describe the seasonal and spatial variation in CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across key subarctic and boreal environmental gradients. A secondary aim is to examine the environmental drivers underlying these flux patterns. We measured fluxes during the snow-free season of 2024 and 2025 in northern Finland, starting early June (spring snowmelt) and ending late September (first snowfall). We conducted 1272 chamber measurements at 144 locations spanning eight high-latitude land cover classes: bare tundra, dwarf-shrub tundra, deciduous forest, evergreen forest, fen, bog, permafrost bog and tundra wetland. Bare tundra, dwarf-shrub tundra, deciduous forest and evergreen forest sites acted as net CH 4 sinks (mean flux of −0.16 to −0.05 mgm-2h-1, depending on land cover class) and as both N 2 O sources and sinks (−0.69 to 1.69 µgm-2h-1). Fen, bog, permafrost bog and tundra wetland sites were net CH 4 sources (mean flux of 0.93 to 27.81 mgm-2h-1) and net N 2 O sinks (−0.89 to −6.53 µgm-2h-1). Highest mean CH 4 fluxes occurred in fens (23.4 mgm-2h-1) and permafrost bogs (27.8 mgm-2h-1) which often coincided with substantial N 2 O sinks (mean flux of −6.53 in fens and −5.40 µgm-2h-1 in permafrost bogs). Seasonal trends were present for CH 4 but were land cover-dependent, with both sinks and sources typically peaking during July–August. Land cover class, soil temperature, and soil pH had the strongest effects on CH 4 fluxes while variation in N 2 O was best explained by soil pH and land cover class. However, a significant portion of the variability in N 2 O remained unexplained. These results demonstrate that strong spatial heterogeneity and pronounced seasonal dynamics during the snow-free period generate substantial variability in CH 4 and N 2 O fluxes across high-latitude ecosystems. Our findings suggest that monthly measurements of insitu gas fluxes and soil conditions in combination with accurate land cover mapping are essential for modelling and upscaling of GHG fluxes. This is especially important in high-latitude regions, where rapid warming is altering both ecosystem distributions and soil conditions with significant consequences for current and future GHG budgets.

articles.title: The operational 3DEnVar data assimilation scheme for the Météo-France convective scale model AROME-France
articles.titleEn: The operational 3DEnVar data assimilation scheme for the Météo-France convective scale model AROME-France
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Since October 2024 the Météo-France operational convective scale model AROME-France has been using a 3DEnVar data assimilation (DA) scheme in order to improve the performance of severe weather prediction. This paper describes the configuration and evaluation of this 3DEnVar scheme. It summarizes the work carried out to configure this scheme in an operational context, with the inherent constraints of numerical robustness, compatible execution times, and of course correct performance of the forecasts produced. The adjustment of horizontal and vertical localization, inflation, hybridization, and the use of Incremental Analysis Updates (IAU) are studied in sensitivity experiments, and the impact on the spin-up is investigated. A configuration and its variation with IAU are thus defined and evaluated using different scores over a long period and on different severe meteorological situations (winter storms, fog, and High Precipitating Events): they largely outperform the operational 3D-Var. The version with IAU was implemented in the new operational version of the AROME-France assimilation system.

articles.title: Scaling and exceedance probability of sinkhole collapse in evaporite karst (Dead Sea, Jordan)
articles.titleEn: Scaling and exceedance probability of sinkhole collapse in evaporite karst (Dead Sea, Jordan)
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Quantitative analysis of sinkhole collapse hazard requires robust data in both space and time. It also needs a clear understanding of the factors and processes that contribute to observed sinkhole locations and dimensions. In many karst settings, these criteria are difficult to meet because of the millennia-long time scales over which sinkhole populations are generated and because of uncertainties around how geomorphological processes link to sinkhole dimensions. This study presents new data on the scaling and probability of sinkhole formation in evaporite karst on the eastern Dead Sea shore (Jordan). Several thousand cover collapse sinkholes have formed there in the past 40 years with minimal post-collapse modification. Genetic processes and timescales are thus well constrained. Utilising high-resolution satellite imagery (Pleiades, PNEO) from 2017–2024, integrated with prior datasets, we present an updated inventory of sinkhole occurrence, extent and dimensions through time over the period 1992–2024. The sinkhole number increased by 43 % from 1565 in 2018 to 2247 in 2024, reflecting a 22 % increase in the sinkhole-affected land area to ca. 179 610 m 2 (17.9 ha). Formation of new karst subsidence features has continued a northward and seaward advance, consistent with control from the decline of the Dead Sea base level. However, we also observed a localised revival in 2021–2022 of sinkhole formation in an area that had been apparently inactive since 2002. This combination of continued and renewed sinkhole formation poses significant challenges to agriculture, housing and infrastructure in the area. Sinkhole average diameters range from 1.1 to 72.9 m; their frequency follows a log-normal distribution, rather than a power-law. Representative annualised exceedance probabilities for formation of sinkholes with diameters greater than 5, 10 and 50 m are ca. 70 %, 30 % and 0.5 % respectively. Exceedance probabilities show slight dependence on sampling time interval and on the nature of near-surface materials in which sinkholes form. Given their log-normal size distribution, the Dead Sea cover collapse sinkholes are not scale-free; instead they are scale-bound by the evaporite karst system's geometrical and mechanical properties.

articles.title: Improving Global Simulation of Irrigation Within the Land Information System
articles.titleEn: Improving Global Simulation of Irrigation Within the Land Information System
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Irrigated agriculture increases evapotranspiration and near surface humidity, decreases air and ground temperatures, augments downwind precipitation, enhances recharge, and depletes surface water and/or groundwater resources. However, model developers have been slow to incorporate irrigation. Using the latest satellite‐based land cover and irrigation data sets and innovative modeling approaches, we developed a scheme for simulating irrigation in the Land Information System (LIS). We reconciled global and national irrigation, land cover, and crop class databases in an effort to (a) distinguish irrigated and rainfed agriculture, (b) approximate fractional crop cover in each model grid pixel, and (c) apply the most likely irrigation method based on the crop class and country or state level information on the relative usage of sprinkler, furrow, paddy, and drip irrigation. Each irrigation method is represented by a separate algorithm. We used agricultural water withdrawal data, as available, for calibration and evaluation. The results compare favorably with available observational and reported data in terms of patterns. The simulated mean annual global irrigation rate, 2,765 km 3 /yr, is on par with an observational estimate (2,500 km 3 /yr) and other irrigation simulating models (mean 2,700 km 3 /yr). Over the contiguous U.S., based on county level reported irrigation water usage data, the new scheme had a root mean square error of 0.22 km 3 while correctly simulating the occurrence of irrigation in 3,053 of 3,220 irrigated counties, compared with 0.24 km 3 /yr and 2,334 counties for LIS's original scheme. Irrigation is estimated to increase global evapotranspiration by 1,700 km 3 /yr (2.4%), similar to a recent independent estimate.

articles.title: Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
articles.titleEn: Antiferroelectric hafnia down to the 2D limit
articles.abstract: Antiferroelectricity is a material property characterized by alternating electric dipoles spontaneously ordered in antiparallel directions. Antiferroelectrics are promising for energy storage, solid-state cooling, and memory technologies; however, these materials are scarce, and their scalability remains largely unexplored. In this work, we demonstrated that single-crystalline hafnia, a lead-free complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)–compatible material, exhibits antiferroelectricity under compressive-strain conditions. We observed antiparallel sublattice polarization and stable double hysteresis in single-crystalline (111)-oriented epitaxial lanthanum (La)–doped hafnia films grown on yttrium-stabilized zirconia and showed that the antipolar orthorhombic phase of hafnia adheres to the Kittel model of antiferroelectricity. Compressive strain strengthens the orthorhombic order in thinner La-doped hafnia films, achieving a very high ordering temperature of 850°C in the two-dimensional limit, highlighting hafnia’s potential for advanced antiferroelectric devices.

articles.title: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
articles.titleEn: Poisoned hunting weapons, megafauna, and plant use at a 125,000-year-old Arabian paleolakeshore
articles.abstract: After the African origin of Homo sapiens , multiple dispersals radiated into Asia, yet the Saharo-Arabian archaeological record remains sparse. In this study, we report on ‘Uruq Aljelibah, a Middle Paleolithic site dated to ~125,000 years ago (marine isotope stage 5e) and located on the shore of Mundafan paleolake, Saudi Arabia. Levallois assemblages, refits, and megafaunal associations indicate in situ tool production and carcass processing. Stone tool residues, use-wear, and biomarkers reveal animal and plant processing, including palms, tubers, trees, and shrubs. Several points exhibit impact damage and poison residues (from Acokanthera schimperi ), indicating use as hafted weapon tips within composite hunting systems. Megafaunal remains include hippopotamus, buffalo, gazelle, ostrich, and camel, illuminating hominin use of freshwater and grassland ecosystems.

articles.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
articles.titleEn: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
articles.abstract: In 2025, a Lancet Commission proposed distinguishing clinical obesity, defined by adiposity-related organ dysfunction, from preclinical obesity, defined by excess adiposity with preserved function, and recommended using anthropometric measures beyond body mass index (BMI) to confirm obesity status 1 . Here we report the comparative performance of this framework versus conventional BMI-based classification using prevalence, incidence and mortality data from 844,108 adults across four cohorts in China, the UK, the USA and Spain. Complementing BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio data showed that BMI alone overestimated obesity in 1.2–3.1% and underestimated it in 5.2–8.6% of participants across cohorts. The combined anthropometric definition increased overall obesity prevalence by 3.3–7.4% relative to BMI-based classification. Clinical obesity accounted for 22.7–31.3% of total obesity, with an overall population prevalence of 5.6–10.9%. A large proportion of individuals (between 77.4% and 91.3%) with preclinical obesity at baseline showed no progression to clinical obesity over 10 years. Increased mortality risk was associated with the combined anthropometric definition of obesity, but not with BMI-only obesity. Clinical obesity was associated with substantially higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.69, 95% confidence interval 1.64–1.73), whereas preclinical obesity conferred only modest risk (1.19, 1.14–1.24). These findings support the global adoption of the Lancet Commission diagnostic framework to improve obesity care and policy.

articles.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
articles.titleEn: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
articles.abstract: A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image 1–4 of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features 3,5–7 , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source 8,9 . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

articles.title: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
articles.titleEn: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
articles.abstract: Extreme glacier melt events accelerate mass loss, increase glacier instability, and temporarily increase downstream runoff, potentially alleviating drought conditions. Yet the glacier energy–mass balance in the Geladandong region – a headwater region of the Yangtze River (China's longest river) and one of the source regions feeding Siling Co (Tibet's largest lake) – and its connection to the unprecedented 2022 summer melt remain insufficiently quantified. To address this gap, we integrated in-situ mass balance observations and glacio-meteorological data from a 5700 m monitoring site with an energy-mass balance model and applied a novel dual-threshold framework (based on mean and standard deviation) to identify extreme mass loss/melt events in short-term glacier mass balance records. Our novel methodology identified 2021/22 as a period of extreme mass loss and melt intensity, with melt during the 2022 summer heatwave reaching unprecedented extremes. These heatwaves caused an increase in melt amount of 317.8 mm w.e., amounting to 1.66 and 1.69 times the values recorded for the same period in 2019/20 and 2020/21, respectively. This extreme melt was driven by energy balance anomalies over the glacier surface. In terms of net contributions to the +28.2 W m −2 melt energy anomaly during the three identified heatwave windows, enhanced sensible heat flux was the largest term (+17.0 W m −2 ; 60.3 %), followed by increased net longwave radiation (+14.0 W m −2 ; 49.7 %) and increased net shortwave radiation (+5.1 W m −2 ; 18.1 %) associated with reduced albedo, with negative contributions from latent heat flux and subsurface heat flux. Such anomalies were driven by large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns, specifically the eastward extension and northward displacement of the South Asian High (SAH), together with near-neutral mid-latitude westerlies. This study advances the understanding of glacier mass balance responses to extreme weather and climate events on the central Tibetan Plateau.

articles.title: Combining different views on internal climate variability of temperature over Europe
articles.titleEn: Combining different views on internal climate variability of temperature over Europe
articles.abstract: Internal climate variability (ICV) represents the intrinsic fluctuations within the climate system. Understanding how ICV varies across regions, seasons, and climatic conditions is crucial for detecting externally forced climate change and assessing future climate risks. It can also provide a useful benchmark for assessing climate model performance and the emergence of anthropogenically forced climate change. This study aims to compare ICV estimates obtained using different methods and data types. We focus on seasonal mean near-surface air temperature over Europe, utilizing data from 15 CMIP6 models, a 100-member MPI-ESM large ensemble, and three observational datasets. The ICV estimates are based on pre-industrial control simulations (Pidata), the Hawkins and Sutton (2009) residual-based method (HS09), regression-based removal of external forcings, and a single-model large-ensemble framework. The magnitude of ICV estimates generally decreases from northeastern to southwestern Europe on both annual and seasonal timescales, except during JJA, when the highest estimates shift southward. The highest ICV estimates are observed in DJF and the lowest at the annual timescale. Among all the methods, Pidata generally yields the highest ICV estimates across all seasonal and annual timescales, except during JJA. Based on the HS09 method, the similarity between the model-based estimates and the observations is most pronounced during DJF and at the annual timescale. However, this similarity is weaker when the regression-based method is applied, with the model-based estimates generally exceeding the observation-based ones. The projected changes in ICV show a tendency for reduced (enhanced) values in DJF (JJA). Although a north-south contrast emerges in other seasons, with declining (increasing) ICV in northern (southern) Europe, the overall spatial pattern indicates a reduction in projected ICV estimates across large parts of Europe, except during JJA.

articles.title: Three‐Phase Mobilization of Organic Phosphorus Sustains Phosphorus Bioavailability Under Long‐Term Nitrogen Addition in a Subtropical Plantation
articles.titleEn: Three‐Phase Mobilization of Organic Phosphorus Sustains Phosphorus Bioavailability Under Long‐Term Nitrogen Addition in a Subtropical Plantation
articles.abstract: Nitrogen (N) input is expected to intensify phosphorus (P) limitation in tropical and subtropical forests. However, how soil and microbial processes mobilize P from poorly available pools to sustain soil P bioavailability remains unclear. We conducted a nine‐year experiment with low (20 kg N ha −1 year −1 ) and high (80 kg N ha −1 year −1 ) N addition treatments in a subtropical Moso bamboo ( Phyllostachys edulis ) plantation. We quantified soil P fractions, P‐cycling functional genes, phosphatase activity, P sorption capacity (PSC), iron and aluminum oxides, and plant properties throughout the experiment. Our results reveal three distinct stages in the regulation of soil bioavailable P with prolonged N addition. Phase I: N addition reduces P bioavailability, and labile organic P decomposition becomes the main source of bioavailable P, associated with increased phosphatase activity. Phase II: when labile organic P becomes insufficient to meet P demand, bioavailable P is replenished through the depletion of moderately labile organic P; this is related to decreased PSC and enhanced acid phosphomonoesterases activity. Phase III: stable organic P decreases significantly, jointly sustaining bioavailable P with the depletion of other organic P fractions, alongside a further decrease in PSC and enriched microbial organic acid‐ and phosphatase‐related genes. This study uncovers a novel “three‐phased P supply” model revealed through long‐term observations. These mechanistic insights reveal the pathways of soil P mobilization under continuous N input in a subtropical forest and establish a framework for predicting the buffering capacity of soil P pools in P‐limited ecosystems under global change scenarios.

articles.title: Mineral‐Associated Carbon Accrual Masks Labile Particulate Carbon Loss in Permafrost Region on the Tibetan Plateau
articles.titleEn: Mineral‐Associated Carbon Accrual Masks Labile Particulate Carbon Loss in Permafrost Region on the Tibetan Plateau
articles.abstract: Permafrost regions store vast quantities of soil organic carbon (SOC), yet the future trajectories of functionally distinct SOC fractions across soil depths remain poorly constrained. Integrating depth‐explicit soil fractionation data from 104 sites across the Tibetan permafrost region with a process‐based SOC model, we project century‐scale dynamics of particulate (POC) and mineral‐associated organic carbon (MAOC) under three emission scenarios. We show that MAOC currently comprises 56.5% of regional total SOC stock and remains far from saturation throughout the profile. Consistent with this large stabilization capacity, total SOC was projected to increase over the 21st century under all scenarios, with the largest gains under SSP5‐8.5. However, this positive net gain masked a significant restructuring of SOC fractions. MAOC accumulated across all depths and scenarios, and heavy POC remained comparatively buffered, whereas light POC declined under SSP5‐8.5. The strongest relative light POC losses occurred in the 10–30 cm layers, where warming‐driven decomposition remained strong while plant‐C input compensation weakened. These divergent trajectories indicate a shift toward a “carbon‐rich yet energy‐poor” state, where mineral‐bound carbon increases while the labile particulate pool supporting microbial activity is depleted. Our findings reveal SOC vulnerability in permafrost region is governed by both fraction identity and soil depth, and that net SOC gains can conceal the loss of metabolically active carbon. Incorporating measurable, depth‐resolved SOC fractions into Earth system models is therefore essential for constraining permafrost–climate feedbacks.

articles.title: Intensive Agriculture and Erosion Affect Composition of Soil Organic Matter
articles.titleEn: Intensive Agriculture and Erosion Affect Composition of Soil Organic Matter
articles.abstract: Land‐use changes induced by human activities usually accelerate soil erosion, leading to losses of soil organic matter (SOM). The mechanisms by which cultivation‐associated degradation affects SOM composition via changes of content and quality of particulate (POM), mineral‐associated (MAOM), dissolved organic matter (DOM), and microbial biomass are not elucidated. We investigated the C:N stoichiometry of these fractions, and erosion (using 137 Cs activity) along a chronosequence of cultivation‐associated degradation (0–114 years) in Mollisols. Two‐pool and Bayesian three‐source mixing models estimated contributions of microbial biomass, DOM, and POM to MAOM to the total SOM. Erosion intensity ranged locally from 440 to 4800 t km −2 year −1 , resulting in cumulative soil losses of 11,000 to 320,000 t km −2 over 114 years of cultivation. As cultivation duration and eroded amounts increased, the C/N ratios of POM, MAOM, and DOM declined owing to (i) the faster loss of C than N, (ii) a decrease in C/N with soil depth involved in tillage horizon, and (iii) N input by fertilization. These higher C than N losses reflect that erosion is not the sole process leading to the decline of C stocks, but intensive cultivation also accelerates organic matter mineralization and CO 2 release to the atmosphere. As the C/N ratios of POM and MAOM declined but microbial C/N increased, the estimated contribution of microbial inputs to MAOM increased from 6% to 32%. The Bayesian model partitioned MAOM sources into DOM (8%), microbial (11%), and POM (81%), reinforcing that POM dominates MAOM formation in croplands. Cultivation‐associated degradation led to SOC losses by reducing POM‐C/N and MAOM‐C/N ratios, while erosion strongly accelerated these effects. Furthermore, cultivation‐associated degradation is also based on the limited inputs of organic C as the precursors for MAOM formation by depleting POM. These results from a > 100‐year chronosequence indicate that cultivation‐induced degradation reduces SOM content, while also shifting the MAOM composition progressively towards a greater contribution of microbial C.

articles.title: Fast Formation of Cloud Clusters by Internal Gravity Waves Emitted by Isolated Shallow Cumulus Clouds in the Conditionally Unstable Boundary Layer
articles.titleEn: Fast Formation of Cloud Clusters by Internal Gravity Waves Emitted by Isolated Shallow Cumulus Clouds in the Conditionally Unstable Boundary Layer
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: The study investigates the processes of cumulus cloud (Cu) dissipation and the formation of a cloud cluster under the conditions of the Barbados Oceanographic and Meteorological Experiment using large‐eddy simulations (LES) with 10 and 20 m resolution and spectral bin microphysics. It is shown that Cu developing and dissipating in a conditionally unstable boundary layer generate internal gravity waves (IGWs), with maximum intensity occurring in the inversion layer. Dissipating Cu can be regarded as point‐like sources of IGWs propagating at different angles below, within, and above the inversion layer. The IGWs propagating within the inversion layer are the most intense and exhibit the largest vertical velocity amplitudes. The apparent horizontal wavelength of the IGWs at different altitudes is determined by the superposition of waves propagating at different angles and increases with distance from the source. Typical apparent horizontal wavelengths are about 1.5–2.0 km, with horizontal phase velocities of approximately 2 m s −1 . Vertical velocity fluctuations associated with IGWs coupled with the plums in the subcloud layer trigger the formation of secondary clouds, giving rise to a growing cloud cluster with the distribution of separation distances between nearest neighboring Cu close to observations. The resulting Cu form the cloud cluster consisting from cells resembling Rayleigh–Benard convective cells. Cloud streets develop in the presence of background wind. It is found that even a single sufficiently strong Cu cloud can trigger the formation of a cloud cluster via IGWs. Semi‐analytical considerations are used for the interpretation of results of LES.

articles.title: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
articles.titleEn: A further acceleration of clean energy is needed for global CO2 emissions to peak and decline
articles.abstract: Global fossil fuel CO 2 emissions have grown 0.8% per year on average between 2019 and 2025. Here we project a decrease of 0.4% in 2026, probably as a short-term response to the energy shock triggered by the Iran conflict. Electric vehicles and solar and wind power offset about 64–79% of increasing emissions from demand growth through 2028; acceleration in clean technology deployment is needed to guarantee emissions peak and subsequent decline.

articles.title: Evaluation of sub-daily precipitation variability and its diurnal characteristics in satellite and reanalysis datasets against ground-based observations
articles.titleEn: Evaluation of sub-daily precipitation variability and its diurnal characteristics in satellite and reanalysis datasets against ground-based observations
articles.abstract: The diurnal cycle of precipitation serves as a fundamental diagnostic of the climate system's energy budget and hydrological cycle. Yet comprehensive evaluations of both its regular diurnal and irregular intermittent components across multiple satellite and reanalysis products against extensive ground-based observations remain limited. This study evaluates the boreal summer diurnal cycle across five satellite products and four reanalysis datasets against 6824 ground-based stations over the Northern Hemisphere land regions, complemented by inter-product comparison over quasi-global domain between 60° S and 60° N. Analyses are performed at 3-hourly resolution, combining sub-daily variance decomposition and harmonic analysis with atmospheric moisture budget diagnosis across contrasting precipitation regimes. Ground-based observations indicate sub-daily fluctuations account for 65.6 % of total precipitation variance, with the irregular component dominating over the repeatable diurnal signal, a fraction that all evaluated datasets systematically underestimate. articles.title: Protected Areas Reduce Heat Exposure in Squamates Globally
articles.titleEn: Protected Areas Reduce Heat Exposure in Squamates Globally
articles.abstract: Protected areas (PAs) are central to biodiversity conservation, yet their capacity to buffer species from climate‐driven heat exposure, that is, the duration and frequency of exposure to temperatures exceeding species' critical thermal limits, remains poorly quantified at global scales. Here, we assessed whether squamate reptiles inside PAs experience lower heat exposure than conspecifics in unprotected, human‐modified landscapes, and how this buffering effect varies across latitudes, biomes, and evolutionary lineages. Using biophysical modelling of operative temperatures across 248 species, we show that PAs consistently reduced both annual hours above critical thermal maximum (CT max ) and the frequency of critical days under current and future climatic scenarios (+2°C and + 4°C). We found that under current climate, protected sites had 51 fewer hours above CT max and 3.5 fewer critical days than unprotected sites, and the proportional reduction persisted under +2°C and + 4°C warming scenarios. The buffering effect was most pronounced at low latitudes and tropical biomes, where species already operate close to their thermal limits. Deserts and xeric shrublands, together with tropical grasslands and savannas, emerged as biomes with elevated heat exposure, reinforcing growing concern for arid‐zone reptiles under climate change. Substantial phylogenetic signal in heat exposure indicated that evolutionary history shapes thermal vulnerability beyond geography and biome alone, with the magnitude of PA buffering varying considerably across squamate lineages. Our findings demonstrate that PAs can provide refugia from heat exposure, and that their conservation value under climate change depends on the retention of structurally complex habitats and thermally heterogeneous microhabitats.

articles.title: Using Artificial Intelligence to Optimize Ecological Restoration for Climate and Biodiversity
articles.titleEn: Using Artificial Intelligence to Optimize Ecological Restoration for Climate and Biodiversity
articles.abstract: The restoration of degraded ecosystems is critical for mitigating climate change and reversing biodiversity loss. Depending on the primary objective—such as maximizing carbon sequestration or protecting threatened species—and within the boundaries of budget limitations, different spatial priorities have been identified at global and regional scales. Funding mechanisms to support such work comprise public sources, philanthropy, and the private sector, including the sale of carbon and biodiversity credits. However, effectively exploring trade‐offs among restoration objectives and estimating the price of biodiversity and carbon credits to design financially viable projects remains scientifically challenging. Here we harness the power of artificial intelligence implemented in the software CAPTAIN to identify spatial priorities for ecological restoration that maximize multiple objectives at once and to allow a robust evaluation of biodiversity and climate outcomes. We find through a series of simulations that even low‐to‐moderate consideration of biodiversity in the design of restoration projects leads to the selection of restored areas that disproportionately improve the conservation of threatened species, while the carbon captured is only slightly reduced. We propose the bundling of biodiversity and carbon credits to support restoration efforts even in areas previously excluded for economic reasons. Applying our methodology to plant diversity in the Atlantic Forest of eastern South America, one of the most biodiverse and threatened ecosystems globally, we demonstrate its potential to guide restoration and to quantify trade‐offs between multiple optimization scenarios. Our study provides a robust, scalable method to maximize the joint benefits of ecological restoration for climate and nature.

articles.title: Projected Climate Change Impacts on Deep‐Sea Corals of the Red Sea
articles.titleEn: Projected Climate Change Impacts on Deep‐Sea Corals of the Red Sea
articles.abstract: Ocean warming, acidification, and deoxygenation, among other co‐occurring factors, are shifting species ranges throughout the marine environment. Mesophotic and deep corals are understudied in their response to climate changes, particularly in the Red Sea, which has relatively high temperatures and salinities and is projected to undergo major changes in the future, with little assessment of the impacts to date. Ecological niche modelling can be used to explain the known distribution of a species, predict its current range, and estimate future range shift under changing ocean scenarios. Here, we estimate the area of suitable habitat for four mesophotic and deep‐sea corals ( Acanthogorgia spp., Stylaster tritoni, Bathypathes thermophila , and Madracis interjecta ) across the whole Red Sea under present conditions and under different scenarios of future environmental changes (years 2090–2100). We found variations in the responses of these corals, but two of the four taxa are projected to lose significant amounts of their current habitats, while the other two lose a smaller portion. In particular, the scleractinian coral M. interjecta is likely to lose the largest proportion of its habitat, while the black coral B. thermophila may experience the least change. Deeper areas may become suitable for these corals, but colonisation will depend on their ability to disperse. We also assessed the potential biodiversity hotspots both now and in the future, finding the northern Red Sea to be one ecologically important area. These results enable marine spatial planning in support of an effective long‐term conservation action to protect these important habitats.

articles.title: Exploring Air–Sea Interactions in a Regional Weakly Coupled Data Assimilation System: An Observing System Experiment for the 2023 Indian Ocean Monsoon and Cyclone Biparjoy
articles.titleEn: Exploring Air–Sea Interactions in a Regional Weakly Coupled Data Assimilation System: An Observing System Experiment for the 2023 Indian Ocean Monsoon and Cyclone Biparjoy
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: We examined air–sea interactions in a weakly coupled ocean–atmosphere data assimilation (DA) system by performing an observing system experiment (OSE). The OSE is performed for the Arabian Sea monsoon onset event in 2023, which also coincides with the passage of the tropical cyclone Biparjoy. Results show that assimilating both oceanic and atmospheric data produces a better forecast of the ocean–atmosphere state (fit to the assimilated data) than either experiment assimilating only oceanic or atmospheric data. This indicates that the coupled system provides more consistent initial conditions, yielding more balanced oceanic and atmospheric states when assimilating all the data. However, we found that assimilating only atmospheric data improves both the ocean and atmosphere state forecasts, whereas assimilating only oceanic data improves the ocean state forecasts but degrades the atmospheric state forecasts, when compared with the free run (coupled model simulation without assimilating any data). We found that this counterintuitive model performance is due to the systematic misrepresentation of air–sea exchanges. First, errors in the cyclone path increase when atmospheric data are not assimilated. Then, assimilation of sea surface temperature (SST) leads to a warmer SST below the misplaced cyclone (with cyclone path offset of about 200 km relative to IBTrACS data), resulting in increased cyclone intensity. This misrepresentation of air–sea exchanges not only occurs during the cyclone passage but also persists throughout the early monsoon season. Since errors in one component can affect the other and result in positive feedback, leading to error growth, this study highlights an interesting effect on weakly coupled ocean–atmosphere DA systems when atmospheric data are unavailable or limited in space and time, particularly during high‐impact atmospheric events such as tropical cyclones.

articles.title: Improvement of a Regional Multiscale NLS‐4DVar Assimilation System Based on the CWRF‐CoLM Coupled Model
articles.titleEn: Improvement of a Regional Multiscale NLS‐4DVar Assimilation System Based on the CWRF‐CoLM Coupled Model
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Ensemble perturbations in 4DEnVar‐type methods are pulled in two directions at once: estimating a reliable background‐error covariance (BEC) calls for perturbations large enough to sample real error structure, while a valid tangent‐linear (TL) approximation calls for perturbations small enough to stay near‐linear. This study resolves this conflict by introducing a shrinkage factor () into a multigrid NLS‐4DVar framework, decoupling the perturbation scale used for BEC estimation from that used for TL approximation. An independent finite‐difference test verifies this decoupling, showing that TL accuracy is governed by a trade‐off between nonlinear truncation error and numerical error. Based on this framework, an improved Regional Multiscale Nonlinear Least Squares (NLS) 4DVar Data Assimilation System was developed based on the CWRF‐CoLM coupled model. A 1‐month cycling assimilation experiment (July 2021) shows that the new scheme (DA2) outperforms the original (DA1): analysis RMSE and bias are reduced for U / V winds, T , and QVAPOR, 3‐day forecast RMSE improves broadly, and the 24‐hr precipitation threat score at moderate‐to‐heavy rainfall thresholds is notably higher, which is consistent with a preferential benefit for strongly nonlinear moisture and convective processes. Although only atmospheric observations are assimilated, land‐surface forecasts (2‐m temperature, 2‐m humidity, soil moisture) also improve indirectly, driven by a more accurate initial moisture field and better‐represented land‐atmosphere coupling. Beyond its practical performance, this decoupling strategy completes a previously unverified aspect of the NLS‐4DVar formulation and offers a generalizable approach for mitigating nonlinear errors in ensemble‐based variational assimilation.

articles.title: Elevated early Eocene atmospheric CO2 tied to reduced Southern Ocean biological pump efficiency
articles.titleEn: Elevated early Eocene atmospheric CO2 tied to reduced Southern Ocean biological pump efficiency
articles.abstract: The Early Eocene Climatic Optimum (53 to 49 million years ago) was an interval in Earth’s history when reconstructed temperatures and atmospheric CO 2 concentrations were among the highest of the Cenozoic Era (that is, the last 66 million years). The causes of the high CO 2 levels remain unclear. CO 2 changes over recent ice age cycles appear to be largely controlled by the biologically mediated build-up and release of carbon from the Southern Ocean, a process that might have also played a role earlier in the Cenozoic. Here we test this possibility with foraminifera-bound nitrogen isotope measurements. Our data show higher surface nitrate concentrations in the Southern Ocean, and thus a more inefficient biological sequestration of carbon during peak Early Eocene Climatic Optimum. The associated transfer of CO 2 from the deep ocean to the atmosphere would have been amplified by the low seawater buffering capacity of the Eocene, due to the lower pH and high Ca ion concentration. Previously proposed low silicate rock weatherability during the Eocene may have weakened the weathering thermostat, allowing the reconstructed change in biological pump efficiency in the Southern Ocean to explain at least half of the atmospheric CO 2 increase observed during the Early Eocene Climatic Optimum.

articles.title: Past and future projected radiative effects from irrigation
articles.titleEn: Past and future projected radiative effects from irrigation
articles.abstract: Irrigation is the most dominant freshwater use practice on Earth, yet its effect on the top-of-atmosphere (TOA) radiative budget remains uncertain because past estimates have relied on idealised experiments or single-model frameworks. Here, we use historical simulations (1902–2014) from the Irrigation Model Intercomparison Project (IRRMIP) to provide the first multi-model quantification of irrigation-induced effective radiative forcing (ERF), defined as the change in net TOA radiative flux including rapid atmospheric adjustments. Across seven Earth system models, under prescribed sea surface temperatures (SST), the global multi-model mean (MMM) irrigation-induced ERF is positive but small (∼ 0.023 W m −2 ). While the global signal is small, it masks regional heterogeneity: South Asia and West Central Asia exhibit higher positive ERF (∼0.23 W m −2 ), with spatial maps revealing coherent forcing hotspots of up to +5 W m −2 over the Indo-Gangetic Plain that are consistent across all models, while East Asia shows negative ERF (∼-0.03 W m −2 ). The clear-sky ERF is greater than the all-sky ERF in most of the regions, indicating that cloud adjustments following irrigation may exert a negative contribution to the ERF. Correlations between historical irrigation ERF variability and its potential drivers suggest that reduced outgoing longwave radiation is the dominant control at the global scale, as well as in South Asia and West Central Asia, while near-surface temperature, precipitable water, albedo, and cloud cover contribute with substantial regional and inter-model variability. We additionally examine future changes in net TOA radiation imbalance (Δ R n,TOA ) from a fully coupled CMIP-style model (SSP1-2.6 and SSP3-7.0, 2015–2070) to assess whether the historical ERF pattern persists under future irrigation. The global mean Δ R n,TOA is more positive under the high irrigation demand pathway (SSP3-7.0) than under SSP1-2.6, consistent with projected differences in irrigation expansion between scenarios. These results demonstrate that irrigation's radiative influence, while small in the global mean, is regionally substantial and scenario-dependent, with implications for the attribution of regional climate change and for the design of land-based mitigation trajectories.

articles.title: Global-scale meteorological-to-groundwater drought propagation and the drivers and patterns of multi-year groundwater drought
articles.titleEn: Global-scale meteorological-to-groundwater drought propagation and the drivers and patterns of multi-year groundwater drought
articles.abstract: Groundwater stores a third of all global freshwater and supports water supply, irrigation and ecosystems across the world. As such, groundwater drought can have wide-reaching financial, social and environmental impacts, particularly when drought events are prolonged or multi-year. Although recent work has made significant progress in understanding the drivers and patterns of multi-year meteorological droughts, we do not know how this signal translates into multi-year groundwater drought, where subsurface processes, anthropogenic influences and abstractions can alter the meteorological signal. This is particularly true at the global-scale, where a major barrier to understanding large-scale groundwater drought dynamics is the difficulty of obtaining consistent and comprehensive groundwater data. In this research, we use a new global hyper-resolution (∼1 km) groundwater dataset to investigate the global patterns and drivers of groundwater drought from 1960–2019, with a specific focus on multi-year events. We start by characterizing the propagation of meteorological (represented by SPEI-12) to groundwater drought, evaluating how and to what extent the sub-surface plays a role in modulating the meteorological drought signal. Subsequently, we define three global groundwater response types that provide a framework for understanding the processes and geo-physical drivers of normal versus multi-year groundwater droughts. We find that 35 % of global groundwater grid cells have an average groundwater drought duration which is multi-year. In 83 % of these locations, the subsurface extends the meteorological drought signal, whereas in the remaining 17 %, groundwater drought duration appears to be primarily driven by meteorological anomalies. Our analysis offers new insights into global-scale drought exposure by identifying regions which have been most vulnerable to multi-year groundwater drought in the past, as well as those which might be more vulnerable in the future. Importantly, our typology also highlights areas where multi-year groundwater droughts can be anticipated based on meteorological drought anomalies and can therefore inform strategies for managing and mitigating future water scarcity risks.

articles.title: On combining climate models into weighted ensembles
articles.titleEn: On combining climate models into weighted ensembles
articles.abstract: Several methods have been proposed and used to refine estimates of future climate change based on combined output from comprehensive climate models. While previously the so-called model democracy approach was used to combine model outputs, where every model is given equal weight, it is now widely accepted that using model weights that account for model performance and model independence is necessary to obtain more reliable results. However, most existing approaches rely, implicitly or explicitly, on a similar statistical basis, while describing things in different ways. Here we distinguish between approaches that are based on the performance of individual models (individual performance weighting) and approaches that are based on the performance of the weighted ensemble as a whole (ensemble performance weighting). At the same time, we formulate both in probabilistic Bayesian terms to make their application and comparison straightforward. Using simple constructed examples, we demonstrate that the ensemble performance weighting approach implicitly accounts for co-dependencies among models, which arguably makes the computation of independence weights for the purpose of model weighting obsolete. We also show that a set of weighted models within the ensemble weighting approach will naturally tend to artificially reduce uncertainty and that this is strongly influenced by the choice of the prior distribution over weight vectors. The distinction between individual and ensemble performance weighting is both methodological and conceptual. Formulating both approaches in general probabilistic Bayesian terms as done here, can serve as a common basis for future developments with regard to ensemble model weighting in Earth system science. The discussed concepts are generally applicable across domains and are thus possibly relevant for other modeling communities as well.

articles.title: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
articles.titleEn: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
articles.abstract: Nuclear conflicts could ignite intense fires that inject considerable amounts of black carbon (BC) into the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere, with the potential to disrupt global climate. While uncertainties in the BC injection remain large, relatively few modeling studies have explored the climatic response to more limited nuclear exchange between major nuclear powers. Here, we investigate the climate response to a set of relatively limited-forcing scenarios (12 to 24 Tg BC) for nuclear exchanges between the United States and Russia. This corresponds to one-tenth to one-fifth of the forcing strength of typically considered. We use the Canadian Earth System Model version 5, an independent contributor to the worldwide set of Earth System Models that has not been explored previously in this application. Consistent with previous work, decreased downwelling shortwave radiation at the surface drives prolonged surface cooling. Unexpectedly, however, a transient surface warming develops in the first boreal summer following a boreal-winter injection, linked to reduced cooling via net longwave and turbulent fluxes. The transient warming is most pronounced for the lowest forcing cases. Precipitation, which decreases even while the surface warms, is found to be controlled by stabilizing, top-heavy warming. Multi-model assessment of these relatively limited-forcing cases is warranted given their potential impacts.

articles.title: Benchmarking conditioners in Liang–Kleeman Information Flow: application to land–atmosphere interactions in humid forests
articles.titleEn: Benchmarking conditioners in Liang–Kleeman Information Flow: application to land–atmosphere interactions in humid forests
articles.abstract: The Liang–Kleeman Information Flow (LKIF) framework has been increasingly used to identify causality in Earth–system dynamics in recent years. Yet, uncertainties remain regarding how the causal graph changes when mediators and confounders (conditioners) are introduced, i.e., divergence between the bivariate and conditioned forms. A controlled synthetic experiment shows that LKIF preserves correct causal directions under hidden confounding, while differences between bivariate and multivariate estimates still occur. We characterize these differences using time-varying LKIF and introduce several quantifiers, including Conditioner Dominance Index, Moderation Gain, Conditioning Pressure, and Convergence Rate, to evaluate the contributions of conditioners. This is illustrated in an application to soil moisture (SM) and vapor pressure deficit (VPD) couplings with vegetation (leaf area index (LAI) and gross primary productivity (GPP)) in humid forest regions of Southeast China and the Amazon Basin, using satellite-derived and reanalysis data over 1981–2018. We find that the influence of SM on LAI remains consistently stable and shows little sensitivity to the selected conditioners, whereas its influence on GPP and that of VPD on vegetation exhibit substantial divergence between bivariate and multivariate estimates. This divergence peaks under compound dry–hot conditions, with VPD and temperature emerging as dominant conditioners. These results demonstrate that bivariate and multivariate LKIF can yield markedly different conclusions across time and space, especially under compound environmental stress. More importantly, even for the same variables in a causal graph, the same conditioners can affect the temporal evolution of the causal relationships very differently at different locations. This highlights how stationary assumptions may oversimplify causal structure by masking relevant temporal transitions, particularly under compound environmental stress.
